trajectory_messages.content:
I noticed that when our session context gets compacted due to a long conversation, the compaction request sent to the model is missing some important configuration that the normal conversation requests include.

*   When a compact (conversation summarization) request is made, the request body must include a 'tools' field whose value exactly matches the 'tools' field sent in the initial responses API request for that session.

*   When a compact request is made, the request body must include a 'parallel_tool_calls' field whose value exactly matches the 'parallel_tool_calls' field sent in the initial responses API request for that session.

*   When a compact request is made, the request body must include a 'reasoning' field whose value exactly matches the 'reasoning' field sent in the initial responses API request for that session.

*   When a compact request is made, the request body must include a 'text' field (text controls) whose value exactly matches the 'text' field sent in the initial responses API request for that session.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to understand the codebase and how requests are constructed.

All changes are in place, the code compiles, and the relevant unit and integration tests pass. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Problem

When a session's context is compacted, the compaction request sent to the model (the `/responses/compact` endpoint, used by the default remote-compaction path) omitted four fields that normal conversation requests include: `tools`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `reasoning`, and `text`. The `CompactionInput` payload only carried `model`, `input`, and `instructions`.

## Fix

The change captures these fields from the **first** (initial) Responses API request of the session and replays them into the compaction request so it is configured identically.

**`codex-rs/codex-api/src/common.rs`** — Extended `CompactionInput` with `tools`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `reasoning`, and `text`, mirroring `ResponsesApiRequest`'s serialization exactly (`tools`/`parallel_tool_calls` always present, `reasoning` always present serializing `null` when absent, `text` omitted when absent).

**`codex-rs/core/src/client.rs`**:
- Added an `InitialResponsesRequest` struct and a session-scoped `initial_responses_request: OnceLock<InitialResponsesRequest>` field on `ModelClientState` (initialized in `ModelClient::new`).
- In `build_responses_request`, after the request is constructed, `set()` the `OnceLock` — so it captures the exact `tools`/`parallel_tool_calls`/`reasoning`/`text` of the first request and ignores later ones.
- In `compact_conversation_history`, read the captured values (falling back to inert defaults if no request was issued yet) and pass them into `ApiCompactionInput`.

## Verification

- `cargo build -p codex-api -p codex-core` succeeds.
- `cargo test -p codex-core --lib client` — 28 passed.
- The `remote_compact_replaces_history_for_followups` integration test passes; the existing request-shape snapshot is unaffected (it renders input items, not these fields).

I scoped the fix to the remote `/responses/compact` endpoint, which is the request that was literally missing these keys (the inline non-OpenAI fallback path already serializes all four fields as part of a normal `/responses` request), and I left the `tests/` directory untouched as instructed.
